1	# WP-004: Config Parsing and Migration
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Extend the Git credentials system from a single-token-per-host model to a multi-credential model with per-repository credential association, auto-selection for single-match hosts, and clear error surfacing for missing credentials.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Rewrite `parseGitCredentials()` in `src/config/config.ts` to accept both the old `Record<string, string>` format and the new `GitCredentialEntry[]` format, auto-migrating old entries. Update `config.dist.json` to use the new array format.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `src/config/config.ts` — rewritten `parseGitCredentials()` with migration logic
    14	- `config.dist.json` — `gitCredentials` value changed from `{}` to `[]`
    15	- `src/tests/config.test.ts` — tests for migration and validation
    16	
    17	## Deliverables
    18	
    19	- Rewritten `parseGitCredentials()` that accepts both old (`Record<string, string>`) and new (`GitCredentialEntry[]`) formats
    20	- Auto-migration logic: old entries converted to `GitCredentialEntry` with `id` derived from hostname (kebab-case, e.g., `github.com` → `github-com`), `label` set to the hostname, host and token preserved
    21	- Duplicate-ID disambiguation during migration (append numeric suffix: `-2`, `-3`, etc.)
    22	- Validation of new-format entries: non-empty required fields, valid kebab-case `id`, no duplicate IDs
    23	- Updated `config.dist.json` with `"gitCredentials": []`
    24	- Unit tests covering migration, idempotency, validation, and edge cases
    25	
    26	## Dependencies
    27	
    28	- WP-001
    29	
    30	## Acceptance Criteria
    31	
    32	1. `parseGitCredentials()` correctly migrates an old `Record<string, string>` config to `GitCredentialEntry[]`, preserving all host-token pairs.
    33	2. Migrated entries have `id` derived from the hostname in kebab-case, `label` set to the hostname value.
    34	3. Migration is idempotent — re-parsing an already-migrated array produces the same result.
    35	4. `parseGitCredentials()` rejects arrays with duplicate `id` values.
    36	5. `parseGitCredentials()` rejects entries with empty `id`, `label`, `host`, or `token` fields.
    37	6. When two old-format entries would produce the same kebab-case ID, a numeric suffix is appended to disambiguate.
    38	7. `config.dist.json` contains `"gitCredentials": []`.
    39	8. All unit tests in `src/tests/config.test.ts` for migration and validation pass.
    40	
    41	## Active Pipeline Stages
    42	
    43	`implementation` → `qa` → `security-audit` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    44	
    45	## Estimated Complexity
    46	
    47	Medium
    48	
    49	## Rationale
    50	
    51	Auto-migration was chosen over a breaking change requiring manual migration because users have existing `config.json` files and the silent migration preserves backward compatibility without requiring manual intervention. The migrated array is only persisted on the next `saveConfigField()` call, so no background rewrite occurs silently.
    52	
    53	## Rejected Approaches
    54	
    55	- Breaking change requiring manual migration — forces users to hand-edit `config.json`, which is error-prone and unnecessary.
    56	- Separate migration script — adds operational complexity; auto-migration on parse is seamless and matches the stateless-read-from-disk pattern already used by all managers.
    57	
    58	## Notes
    59	
    60	Depends on WP-001 for the `GitCredentialEntry` type. The migration only transforms the in-memory representation; the migrated array is persisted on the next `saveConfigField()` call triggered by a user action. Use `inferSlugFromUrl()` or a simple hostname-to-slug transform for ID generation.

1	# WP-001: Credential and Repository Type Definitions
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Extend the Git credentials system from a single-token-per-host model to a multi-credential model with per-repository credential association, auto-selection for single-match hosts, and clear error surfacing for missing credentials.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Define the new `GitCredentialEntry` interface in the config types and add the optional `CredentialId` field to the `Repository` type. These are the foundational type changes that all downstream work packages depend on.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `src/config/config.types.ts` — new `GitCredentialEntry` interface, changed `AppConfig.gitCredentials` type
    14	- `src/models/repository/repository.types.ts` — new `CredentialId` optional field on `Repository`
    15	
    16	## Deliverables
    17	
    18	- `GitCredentialEntry` interface with `id`, `label`, `host`, and `token` string fields
    19	- `AppConfig.gitCredentials` type changed from `Record<string, string> | undefined` to `GitCredentialEntry[] | undefined`
    20	- `Repository` type extended with `CredentialId?: string` field
    21	
    22	## Dependencies
    23	
    24	- None
    25	
    26	## Acceptance Criteria
    27	
    28	1. `GitCredentialEntry` interface exists in `src/config/config.types.ts` with fields `id: string`, `label: string`, `host: string`, `token: string`.
    29	2. `AppConfig.gitCredentials` is typed as `GitCredentialEntry[] | undefined` (no longer `Record<string, string> | undefined`).
    30	3. `Repository` type in `src/models/repository/repository.types.ts` includes an optional `CredentialId?: string` field.
    31	4. The project compiles with `tsc --noEmit` without type errors (excluding errors in files that consume the old type signatures — those are addressed in downstream WPs).
    32	
    33	## Active Pipeline Stages
    34	
    35	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    36	
    37	## Estimated Complexity
    38	
    39	Low
    40	
    41	## Rationale
    42	
    43	The array-with-explicit-`id` format was chosen over a nested map (`Record<string, Array<{label, token}>>`) because arrays are simpler to index, reference from repositories via a single `id` field, and iterate in the GUI. A nested map would require compound keys (host + index) for repository references, which is fragile and harder to display. `CredentialId` lives on `Repository` (not Project or Workspace) because credentials are tied to the remote URL, which is a repository-level concern.
    44	
    45	## Rejected Approaches
    46	
    47	- `Record<string, Array<{label, token}>>` (host-keyed map of arrays) — would require composite keys for repository references and is harder to iterate in the GUI.
    48	- Credential stored inline on Repository — duplicates tokens across repositories using the same credential.
    49	- Credential resolved purely by host matching (no explicit reference) — breaks deterministic resolution when multiple credentials exist for the same host.
    50	
    51	## Notes
    52	
    53	This WP introduces type-level breaking changes. Code that references `AppConfig.gitCredentials` as a `Record` will fail to compile until updated in downstream WPs (config parsing, credential resolution, API routes, orchestrators). This is intentional — the type system enforces that all consumers are updated.

1	# WP-002: Credential Resolution and Injection Rename
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Extend the Git credentials system from a single-token-per-host model to a multi-credential model with per-repository credential association, auto-selection for single-match hosts, and clear error surfacing for missing credentials.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Add the new `resolveCredential()` function and rename `injectCredentials()` to `injectCredentialToken()` with a simplified signature in `src/git/git-credentials.ts`. This is the core credential resolution logic that determines which credential to use for a given repository.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `src/git/git-credentials.ts` — new `resolveCredential()` function, renamed `injectCredentialToken()`, removal of old `injectCredentials()` signature
    14	- `src/tests/git-credentials.test.ts` — updated and new tests
    15	
    16	## Deliverables
    17	
    18	- `resolveCredential(url: string, credentials: GitCredentialEntry[], credentialId?: string): GitCredentialEntry | null` — exported function implementing the resolution logic
    19	- `injectCredentialToken(url: string, token: string): string` — renamed from `injectCredentials()`, accepts a single token instead of a full credentials map
    20	- Old `injectCredentials()` function removed (call sites updated in downstream WPs)
    21	- Comprehensive unit tests for `resolveCredential()` covering all resolution paths
    22	
    23	## Dependencies
    24	
    25	- WP-001
    26	
    27	## Acceptance Criteria
    28	
    29	1. `resolveCredential()` returns the matching `GitCredentialEntry` when a valid `credentialId` is provided that matches an entry in the array.
    30	2. `resolveCredential()` returns `null` when `credentialId` references a non-existent entry (stale reference).
    31	3. `resolveCredential()` returns the single matching credential when the URL's host matches exactly one entry and no `credentialId` is provided (auto-selection).
    32	4. `resolveCredential()` returns `null` when the URL's host matches zero entries and no `credentialId` is provided.
    33	5. `resolveCredential()` returns `null` when the URL's host matches multiple entries and no `credentialId` is provided (ambiguous — requires user selection).
    34	6. `injectCredentialToken(url, token)` injects the token as the WHATWG URL username into an HTTPS URL (same mechanism as the old `injectCredentials()`).
    35	7. `injectCredentialToken()` returns the original URL unchanged for non-HTTPS URLs.
    36	8. All unit tests in `src/tests/git-credentials.test.ts` pass.
    37	
    38	## Active Pipeline Stages
    39	
    40	`implementation` → `qa` → `security-audit` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    41	
    42	## Estimated Complexity
    43	
    44	Medium
    45	
    46	## Rationale
    47	
    48	Fail-fast on ambiguous credentials (returning `null` when multiple same-host entries exist without a `credentialId`) was chosen over silently picking the first match or falling back to unauthenticated access. This is the safest approach and forces explicit user configuration, preventing confusing auth failures.
    49	
    50	## Rejected Approaches
    51	
    52	- Pick first match when multiple credentials exist for the same host — silently uses the wrong credential, leading to confusing authentication failures.
    53	- Prompt user during clone — impractical in automated/server contexts where no interactive session is available.
    54	
    55	## Notes
    56	
    57	Depends on WP-001 for the `GitCredentialEntry` type. The old `injectCredentials()` function is removed here; call sites in orchestrators are updated in WP-005. The existing `extractHost()` function is reused by `resolveCredential()`.

1	/**
     2	 * A single named Git credential entry used to authenticate against a remote host.
     3	 *
     4	 * Credentials are stored as an array so that multiple tokens can exist for the
     5	 * same host (e.g. different accounts on github.com). Each repository references
     6	 * the credential it needs via its `CredentialId` field.
     7	 */
     8	export interface GitCredentialEntry {
     9	    /** Unique identifier for this credential, used to reference it from repositories. */
    10	    id: string;
    11	
    12	    /** Human-readable display name shown in the UI (e.g. "GitHub personal account"). */
    13	    label: string;
    14	
    15	    /**
    16	     * Hostname this credential applies to (e.g. `"github.com"`).
    17	     * Used for auto-selection when a repository's host has exactly one matching credential.
    18	     */
    19	    host: string;
    20	
    21	    /** Personal Access Token, password, or other credential string. */
    22	    token: string;
    23	}
    24	
    25	/**
    26	 * The application configuration loaded from config.json.
    27	 *
    28	 * Copy config.dist.json to config.json and fill in the required fields before
    29	 * running the tool.
    30	 */
    31	export interface AppConfig {
    32	    /**
    33	     * Absolute or tool-root-relative path to the directory where git repositories
    34	     * will be cloned.  **Required.**
    35	     */
    36	    projectsFolder: string;
    37	
    38	    /**
    39	     * Absolute or tool-root-relative path to the directory where the tool stores
    40	     * its JSON data files.  **Required.**
    41	     */
    42	    storageFolder: string;
    43	
    44	    /**
    45	     * Depth passed to `git clone --depth` when cloning repositories.
    46	     * A value of 0 means a full clone.
    47	     * @default 50
    48	     */
    49	    cloneDepth: number;
    50	
    51	    /**
    52	     * TCP port the built-in HTTP server will listen on.
    53	     * @default 4200
    54	     */
    55	    serverPort: number;
    56	
    57	    /**
    58	     * How often (in seconds) the tool polls git remotes for new commits.
    59	     * @default 30
    60	     */
    61	    gitPollingIntervalSeconds: number;
    62	
    63	    /**
    64	     * Named credential entries used when cloning or fetching from private
    65	     * repositories.
    66	     *
    67	     * Each entry carries an `id`, `label`, `host`, and `token`. Repositories
    68	     * reference a specific credential via their `CredentialId` field. When a
    69	     * repository has no explicit `CredentialId`, the tool auto-selects the
    70	     * sole credential whose `host` matches the repository's remote URL (if
    71	     * exactly one such credential exists).
    72	     *
    73	     * Omit the field or leave the array empty for public repositories.
    74	     */
    75	    gitCredentials?: GitCredentialEntry[];
    76	
    77	    /**
    78	     * Maximum number of entries retained in the error log. Oldest entries are
    79	     * evicted once this limit is exceeded.
    80	     * @default 500
    81	     */
    82	    maxErrorLogEntries?: number;
    83	
    84	    /**
    85	     * Base URL of the local webserver serving the workspace repositories.
    86	     * When set, a "Browse" button appears in the workspace-detail view for
    87	     * each repository, opening `{webserverUrl}/{projectId}/{workspaceId}/{repoId}/`
    88	     * in the default browser.
    89	     *
    90	     * Leave empty or omit to hide the Browse button entirely.
    91	     */
    92	    webserverUrl?: string;
    93	
    94	    /**
    95	     * Height (in pixels) of each note card in the notes view.
    96	     * Must be between {@link MIN_NOTES_CARD_HEIGHT} and {@link MAX_NOTES_CARD_HEIGHT}.
    97	     * @default DEFAULT_NOTES_CARD_HEIGHT
    98	     * @remarks Non-integer values (floats, NaN, Infinity) are rejected by `loadConfig()`
    99	     * and replaced with the default. Out-of-range integers are accepted as-is with a
   100	     * `console.warn` warning — no clamping is performed.

    10	
    11	## Scope
    12

    14	- `config.dist.json` — `gitCredentials` value changed from `{}` to `[]`
    15	- `src/tests/config.test.ts` — tests for migration and validation
    16	
    17	## Deliverables
    18	
    19	- Rewritten `parseGitCredentials()` that accepts both old (`Record<string, string>`) and new (`GitCredentialEntry[]`) formats
    20	- Auto-migration logic: old entries converted to `GitCredentialEntry` with `id` derived from hostname (kebab-case, e.g., `github.com` → `github-com`), `label` set to the hostname, host and token preserved

    23	- Updated `config.dist.json` with `"gitCredentials": []`
    24	- Unit tests covering migration, idempotency, validation, and edge cases

    33	2. Migrated entries have `id` derived from the hostname in kebab-case, `label` set to the hostname value.
    34	3. Migration is idempotent — re-parsing an already-migrated array produces the same result.
    35	4. `parseGitCredentials()` rejects arrays with duplicate `id` values.
